variants.headline: Business plan abandoned before opening
variants.sub: The planned {business} will not open: {founder} has given up the plan.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business} before opening. The reason given is that {why}. The builder keeps what it was paid, and any grant is owed back. For {target}, the result raises a direct question about responsibility before an enterprise can begin operating.

The person behind a business plan remains a person when it is abandoned. Labour should keep the household in view without treating a builder's work as though it never mattered. Fair treatment requires attention to the commitments on both sides, not an easy slogan about who ought to carry the disappointment.

We criticise {target} on the standard of stewardship. A plan that ends before opening still involves real commitments, and responsibility should not disappear merely because the hoped-for enterprise never began operating. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
